purpose: K-1 source resolution for the centella re-cut. A source with resolved:false MAY NOT be cited.
scope_note: Built ONLY from the three candidate sources named in the brief, fetched directly. No other repository or evidence system was consulted.

sources.published_title_verbatim: The effect of Centella Asiatica cream on scar development in patients who underwent open carpal tunnel release surgery.
sources.journal_verbatim: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
sources.scope_verbatim: In the intervention group, a petroleum cream mixture consisting of 1% Centella asiatica extract was applied to the patients' wrist for 6 months after the sutures were removed.
sources.conclusion_verbatim: The Centella asiatica cream applied to the wrist after CTR surgery was found to be beneficial in preventing scar tenderness in the thenar and hypothenar regions of the hand.
sources.escalate: OFF-TOPIC for every claim row in this video. Population is post-operative carpal tunnel release; site is the wrist and hand; outcome is surgical scar (Vancouver Scar Scale, QuickDASH, VAS). Contains nothing on facial skin, barrier function, inflammation signalling, constituent ranking, or a daily cosmetic routine. Recorded, not substituted.

sources.published_title_verbatim: A Systematic Review of the Effect of [Centella asiatica] on Wound Healing
sources.verbatim_note: The PubMed/PMC API strips italicised species names from title and body. The elision is marked in brackets. Uncorrected API string: 'A Systematic Review of the Effect ofon Wound Healing.' Every quotation below carries the same artifact and is marked the same way.
sources.journal_verbatim: International journal of environmental research and public health
sources.trial_count_verbatim: Four studies [,,,] on[Centella asiatica] were included in the systematic review ().
sources.inclusion_scope_verbatim: Oral or topical treatment with[Centella asiatica] for at least 3 weeks.
sources.limitation_verbatim: Only four studies were included in the systematic review, and this may limit the wider application of the findings of the review.

quotable_sentences.four_triterpenes: The main triterpenes found in[Centella asiatica], also known as centelloids, are asiatic acid (AA), asiaticoside (AS), madecassoside (MS) or brahminoside, and madecassic acid (MA) or brahmic acid [,,].
quotable_sentences.common_names: [Centella asiatica], also known as Gotu Kola, Bua-bok, Tiger grass, or Indian Pennywort [,], is an herbaceous perennial plant member of the[Apiaceae] family, also known as[Umbelliferae].
quotable_sentences.most_active_constituent: These wound healing properties appear particularly effective when the extract contains greater amounts of AS [], being one of its more active compounds.
quotable_sentences.fibroblast_proliferation: In addition, the enhanced proliferation of fibroblasts and the synthesis of the extracellular matrix has been reported after treatment with AS [].
quotable_sentences.anti_inflammatory: [Centella asiatica] has shown an anti-inflammatory effect observed by the reduction in Interleukin-1β (IL-1β), Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and Tumour Necrosis Factor α (TNFα) [,,], as well as prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) [,], and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) [].

supports_rows: R7 (RE-SCOPED: anti-inflammatory effect, in wound healing)
sources.escalate: SCOPE MISMATCH against the brief. The brief specified 'the 4-trial PRISMA systematic review of TOPICAL centella'. This review is 4-trial and PRISMA, but its inclusion criterion is 'Oral or topical treatment', and two of its four trials are ORAL (oral asiaticoside capsules; oral CA tablets). No topical-only 4-trial PRISMA review of centella was found -- see not_found below. Included as the nearest real object with its true scope stated, NOT as a silent substitution.
sources.row_R7_supporting_sentence_verbatim: [Centella asiatica] has shown an anti-inflammatory effect observed by the reduction in Interleukin-1β (IL-1β), Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and Tumour Necrosis Factor α (TNFα) [,,], as well as prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) [,], and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) [].
sources.row_R7_scope_guard: R7 was re-scoped by operator instruction to the limb this sentence supports, and the on-screen type carries 'IN WOUND HEALING' plus a following scene stating the review is not about daily skincare. The fibroblast and barrier limbs were NOT sourced and were removed, not softened.

sources.published_title_verbatim: Safety Assessment of Centella asiatica-derived Ingredients as Used in Cosmetics
sources.fetch_method: curl -> pypdf text extraction (24 pages, 77,393 chars)
sources.draft_check: CONFIRMED the Jul 2015 FINAL, not the Feb 2015 draft: the cover page prints 'Status: Final Report' and 'Release Date: July 10, 2015'. The filename's '06' is the Panel Date (June 15-16, 2015), not the release.
sources.conclusion_verbatim: The CIR Expert Panel concluded that the following 9 ingredients are safe in the present practices of use and concentration in cosmetics, as described in this safety assessment, when formulated to be non-sensitizing.
sources.term_scan_note: Full-text term scan over all 24 pages. The 7 'fibroblast' hits concern asiatic acid INHIBITING collagen type I expression in keloid fibroblasts -- the opposite direction from a 'fibroblasts rebuild' claim. The report names asiatic acid as 'one of the active constituents', never madecassoside as primary.
sources.escalate: SAFETY SCOPE ONLY. Establishes conditional safety, not efficacy or mechanism. Cannot source any efficacy/mechanism row in this video.

not_found.described_as: The 4-trial PRISMA systematic review of topical centella

searches_run.result: Returned 39233460 (26-plant photoaging cosmeceutical review), 33141449 / 27048768 / 16034893 (Cochrane phlebotonics, 66-69 RCTs, and each states 'No studies evaluating topical phlebotonics ... fulfilled the inclusion criteria'), 10796111 (stretch-mark creams, ONE included study). None is a 4-trial PRISMA review of topical centella.

searches_run.query: Centella asiatica PRISMA systematic review wound healing clinical trials
searches_run.result: Returned 35328954 (= S2, oral or topical) and 39757623 (26 trials, 45 plant species, not centella-specific).

not_found.conclusion: No topical-only 4-trial PRISMA review of centella exists in PubMed under these searches. S2 is the nearest real object and is recorded with its true oral-or-topical scope. MAY NOT be cited as a topical-only review.
